title: checkpoints/<id>.md — YAML frontmatter
$comment: Frontmatter of a checkpoint file; the body is markdown. A checkpoint is a synthesis written against the origin: the latest one is where the thread stands, and all of them in order are its history. The body is an outline whose first line is the headline, then '## Status' and optionally '## Inherited' (at most 3 one-line items, each tagged with the checkpoint it came from). Size limits on the body are checked by the tool, since JSON Schema can't see markdown; `inherited` is mirrored here so it can be checked and rendered without parsing the body. A checkpoint can't record the hash of its own commit; `git log --grep 'checkpoint <id>@<cid>'` finds it.

at.description: The latest event id the author had read. The write succeeds only if it is still the latest; events after it are 'since the last checkpoint'.

headline.description: One line for the thread's history. The cap is enforced at write time.

inherited.description: Mirror of the body's '## Inherited' section, written by the tool: at most 3 one-line items, each tagged with the checkpoint it came from.

since.description: Checkpoint id where this item first appeared.

forced-by.description: Set when a structural moment required the checkpoint rather than the author choosing it.

metadata.description: thread.yml as it stood when the checkpoint was written: the baseline the view diffs against for its 'thread.yml since the last checkpoint' line. Absent in checkpoints written before 09-25.

project-head.description: HEAD of the project containing the threads root, when that parent is a Git repository.
